The permit hearing was scheduled for 6:00 p.m. in a room built for forty and it had been shut since March, which meant the air conditioning had been off for eleven weeks and the carpet had developed opinions of its own. I counted eighty-one people. Twelve of them had signed up to speak. The rest had come to watch, which tells you everything about the entertainment options in a town of 4,300 on a Tuesday in August.

The applicant's attorney arrived at 6:04 in a charcoal suit that cost more than the annual budget for the branch library, carrying a bound presentation with tabs. Tabs. Forty-one pages of tabs, for a request to rezone 62 acres of drainage easement into what the document called, in a font chosen by someone who has never been afraid of anything, a Lifestyle Village.

He spoke for thirty-one minutes. He used the word "synergy" four times and the word "community" nineteen, and at no point did he mention the culvert.

The culvert is the entire question. It runs under County Road 9 at a diameter of 36 inches, it was installed in 1974, and the county's own engineering study — commissioned in 2019, filed in 2021, and never once cited by anyone in that charcoal suit — concludes that it is undersized for current runoff by a factor of roughly two and a half. Pave 62 acres upstream of it and the arithmetic becomes something you can watch happen from your porch.

A woman in the fourth row stood up during the public comment period and said this. She had brought the study. She had tabbed it herself, in yellow, with a highlighter, and she read the relevant paragraph aloud into a microphone that squealed twice and then quit entirely, so she finished the paragraph shouting, which the chairman noted was out of order.

The vote was 4-1. The dissent came from a man who has lost this vote fourteen times in six years and shows up anyway, which is either the most encouraging thing in the county or the most damning, depending on how you feel about arithmetic.

The applicant's attorney was in his car by 8:40. I watched him go. He had a call to make and a two-hour drive back to a city where the drainage is somebody else's problem, and the culvert under County Road 9 is still 36 inches across, and the rain in this part of the state comes in November.

I have the engineering study on the seat beside me. It is 94 pages. Page 61 has a table.
